Let
\[
A_m(a)=\sum_{k=0}^m\frac{(-1)^k\binom mk}{k+a}.
\]
Using
\[
\frac1{k+a}=\int_0^1 x^{k+a-1}\,dx,
\]
we get
\[
A_m(a)=\int_0^1 x^{a-1}(1-x)^m\,dx
=B(a,m+1)=\frac{\Gamma(a)\Gamma(m+1)}{\Gamma(m+a+1)}.
\]
Also
\[
\sum_{k=0}^m\frac{(-1)^k\binom mk}{(k+a)^2}
=-A_m'(a)=A_m(a)H_m(a),
\]
where
\[
H_m(a)=\sum_{j=0}^m\frac1{a+j}.
\]

Write
\[
B_q=e^{q-1}A_{n^q}(a),\qquad H_q=H_{n^q}(a),
\]
and put \(N=n^3\). Since
\[
A_{N+1}(a)=A_N(a)\frac{N+1}{N+1+a},
\]
let
\[
\rho=\frac{N+1}{N+1+a}.
\]
The determinant condition says that the weighted average of the \(H\)'s is unchanged after replacing the third term by \(N+1\). A direct expansion gives the exact equivalent equation
\[
a\{B_1(H_1-H_3)+B_2(H_2-H_3)\}+\rho(B_1+B_2+B_3)=0. \tag{1}
\]

Now set
\[
L=\log n,\qquad s=aL.
\]
The solution satisfies \(|s-1|<1/10\). Uniformly in that range,
\[
A_{n^q}(a)=\Gamma(a)n^{-qa}\left(1-\frac{a(a+1)}{2n^q}+O(n^{-2q})\right).
\]
Thus
\[
\frac{B_q}{\Gamma(a)e^{-1}}
=e^{q(1-s)}\left(1-\frac{a(a+1)}{2n^q}+O(n^{-2q})\right).
\]
Also
\[
H_1-H_3=-2L+\frac{a+\frac12}{n}+O(n^{-2}),
\]
\[
H_2-H_3=-L+O(n^{-2}),
\]
and
\[
\rho=1+O(n^{-3}L^{-1}).
\]

Keeping terms through order \((nL)^{-1}\), write \(s=1+\varepsilon\). Then
\[
\frac{B_1}{\Gamma(a)e^{-1}}=1-\varepsilon-\frac1{2nL}+o((nL)^{-1}),
\]
\[
\frac{B_2}{\Gamma(a)e^{-1}}=1-2\varepsilon+o((nL)^{-1}),
\]
\[
\frac{B_3}{\Gamma(a)e^{-1}}=1-3\varepsilon+o((nL)^{-1}),
\]
and
\[
1+a(H_1-H_3)=-1-2\varepsilon+\frac1{2nL}+o((nL)^{-1}),
\]
\[
1+a(H_2-H_3)=-\varepsilon+o((nL)^{-1}).
\]
Substituting into (1), after division by the positive common factor \(\Gamma(a)e^{-1}\), gives
\[
\left(-1-\varepsilon+\frac1{nL}\right)
+(-\varepsilon)
+(1-3\varepsilon)
+o((nL)^{-1})=0.
\]
Hence
\[
-5\varepsilon+\frac1{nL}+o((nL)^{-1})=0,
\]
so
\[
nL(s-1)\to \frac15.
\]
Since \(s=a_n\log n\), the required limit is
\[
\boxed{\frac15}.
\]
